subject.title: fix(agents): repair double-escaped JSON strings in tool call argument…

question: Should OpenClaw preserve valid parsed command/content strings unless malformed raw-stream provenance is known, even if that leaves intermittent exec corruption unresolved while the shared source is traced?
rationale: The patch must choose between repairing the reported exec cases and preserving legitimate literal escape semantics; the current final-string heuristic cannot safely tell those cases apart.

options.title: Repair at the malformed-stream boundary
options.body: Identify the decoder or fragmented-delta path that introduces extra escaping and apply any normalization only when that corruption is evidenced.

options.title: Narrow the heuristic scope
options.body: Exclude `exec.command` and other ambiguous freeform fields until the runtime has a reliable corruption marker, accepting reduced coverage for the reported cases.

recommendation.title: Repair at the malformed-stream boundary
recommendation.body: Identify the decoder or fragmented-delta path that introduces extra escaping and apply any normalization only when that corruption is evidenced.
